## Docs

* [Phase 00: Project setup](docs/00-project-setup.md) - Goal: a skeleton that runs, has a test command, and has a place for everything we'll add later.
* [Phase 01: Talking to the model](docs/01-talking-to-the-model.md) - Goal: understand that "calling an AI" is just one HTTP request with some JSON.
* [Phase 02: Conversation state and the rich terminal UI](docs/02-conversation-and-the-rich-ui.md) - Goal: chat back and forth, with the model "remembering" earlier messages, in a nice-looking terminal app.
* [Phase 03: Streaming and interrupts](docs/03-streaming-and-interrupts.md) - Goal: show the reply word by word as it's written, let you stop it halfway, and survive temporary API errors.
* [Phase 04: The agent loop](docs/04-the-agent-loop.md) - Goal: turn the chatbot into an agent.
* [Phase 05: A real toolset](docs/05-a-real-toolset.md) - Goal: give the agent the tools it needs to do real work: find files, search inside them, change them, and run commands.
* [Phase 06: Permissions and safety](docs/06-permissions.md) - Goal: put you back in control.
* [Phase 07: Context engineering](docs/07-context-engineering.md) - Goal: decide what the model knows before it starts working.
* [Phase 08: The context window](docs/08-context-window.md) - Goal: keep long sessions working.
* [Phase 09: Sessions and prompt caching](docs/09-sessions-and-caching.md) - Goal: two things.
* [Phase 10: Configuration and custom commands](docs/10-configuration.md) - Goal: stop re-typing flags.
* [Phase 11: Planning and task tracking](docs/11-planning.md) - Goal: keep the model on track during long tasks.
* [Phase 12: Hooks](docs/12-hooks.md) - Goal: run your own code at fixed moments of the agent's work, every time, whatever the model thinks.
* [Phase 13: Subagents](docs/13-subagents.md) - Goal: let the model hand a job to another agent with its own, empty context window, and get back only the answer.
* [Phase 14: MCP, plugging in other people's tools](docs/14-mcp.md) - Goal: use tools that live in other programs (a GitHub client, a database, a browser) without writing them into noobly.
* [Phase 15: Skills and progressive disclosure](docs/15-skills.md) - Goal: give the agent detailed know-how for many kinds of task, without paying for all of it on every request.
* [Phase 16: Memory](docs/16-memory.md) - Goal: let noobly carry knowledge from one session to the next: "I prefer tabs", "run tests with `npm run test:unit`", "never touch `generated/`".
* [Phase 17: Headless mode, the library API, and input polish](docs/17-headless-and-library.md) - Goal: use noobly from scripts and from other programs, not just the chat screen.
* [Phase 18: Robustness and the outside world](docs/18-robustness.md) - Goal: keep working when things go wrong (connections drop, replies get cut off, pages lie), and reach beyond the project: the web, local models, and the model's own thinking.
* [Phase 19: Observability and evals](docs/19-observability-and-evals.md) - Goal: measure the agent.
* [Phase 20: The OS sandbox](docs/20-sandbox.md) - Goal: limit what a command can do, instead of guessing what it will do.
* [Phase 21: Checkpoints & rewind](docs/21-checkpoints-and-rewind.md) - Goal: make every change undoable.
* [Phase 22: Background tasks](docs/22-background-tasks.md) - Goal: let the agent start something that keeps running (a dev server, a watcher, a slow build), carry on working, and check back.
* [Phase 24: Feedback after every edit](docs/24-feedback-after-edits.md) - Goal: the model sees a mistake in the same tool result that made it, not three calls later.
* [Phase 25: Editing tools shaped for the model](docs/25-edit-tools-per-model.md) - Goal: fewer failed edits, by giving each model the edit format it's best at, and forgiving the mistakes that don't matter.
* [Phase 26: Big output without losing it](docs/26-big-output.md) - Goal: a 20,000-line test log shouldn't lose its middle, where the one failing test is.
* [Phase 27: A map of the codebase](docs/27-repo-map.md) - Goal: in a big repo, orient the model in one glance instead of ten searches.
* [Phase 28: Seeing and searching](docs/28-images-and-search.md) - Goal: the model can look at a screenshot, and find a page it wasn't given.
* [Phase 29: Parallel agents in worktrees](docs/29-worktrees.md) - Goal: several subagents editing at the same time, without overwriting each other.
* [Phase 30: Editors and other front-ends](docs/30-editors-acp.md) - Goal: use noobly from inside an editor, without changing the agent loop at all.
* [noobly docs: start here](docs/README.md) - These notes explain, in plain language, everything that has been built so far and why.
* [Extra: Rendering Markdown in the terminal](docs/extra-markdown-rendering.md) - The problem you spotted: models write their answers in Markdown, but noobly printed them as plain text, so you saw the raw symbols:
* [Extra: Anthropic, OpenAI or Grok](docs/extra-multiple-providers.md) - Goal: let noobly use whichever AI company you have an API key for, and let you pick the model.
* [A test scenario for the v2 features](docs/extra-v2-test-scenario.md) - One session that exercises every v2 feature (Phases 20–30) with a real model.
* [Glossary](docs/glossary.md)

## Learning

* [Lesson 1: What is a harness?](learning/01-what-is-a-harness.md) - Forget everything you know about Claude Code, Cursor or noobly.
* [Lesson 2: The model is a function](learning/02-the-model-is-a-function.md) - Before we can build an agent, we need to be precise about the thing we're wrapping.
* [Lesson 3: The agent loop](learning/03-the-agent-loop.md) - This is the most important lesson.
* [Lesson 4: Tools](learning/04-tools.md) - The loop gives the model a way to act.
* [Lesson 5: Control and safety](learning/05-control-and-safety.md) - By now the model can run `Bash`.
* [Lesson 6: Context](learning/06-context.md) - We've covered the loop (how the model acts) and control (what it may do).
* [Lesson 7: The whole picture](learning/07-the-whole-picture.md) - You now have all four jobs: loop, control, context, interface.
* [Harnesses from first principles](learning/README.md) - A short course for getting back in touch with noobly, starting from nothing.

## Specs

* [Architecture — Noobly Learn Harness](specs/Architecture.md) - This document describes the end-state architecture.
* [PRD — Noobly Learn Harness](specs/PRD.md) - `noobly` is a terminal-based AI coding agent, functionally modelled on tools like Claude Code, built progressively so that each stage of the build teaches one core concept of agent harness design.
* [Roadmap — Noobly Learn Harness](specs/Roadmap.md) - The build is split into 5 milestones and 20 phases for v1, plus 3 milestones and 11 phases for v2 (below).
